summary: Well‑executed, artifact‑grounded preregistered paired trial comparing a generate–verify–repair (GVR) pipeline to LLM‑only generation on a 500‑intent synthetic NetOps benchmark. The experiment, analysis, and artifacts are complete and reproducible; the preregistered exact conditional McNemar test is appropriate and reported (n11=496, n10=4, n01=0, p=0.125). Authors correctly avoid a confirmatory claim. Key strengths: preregistration, complete artifact hashes and traces, deterministic verifier semantics, transparent accounting of model calls and repairs. Main weaknesses are clarificatory and reporting gaps (resolvable from archived artifacts): an ambiguous provider_call_audit field, missing concise summary of the four repaired/discordant episodes in the paper body, explicit statement of which preregistered confirmatory comparisons were unexecuted and the consequence for multiplicity, and explicit model-generation hyperparameters. After those manuscript clarifications are made the paper will be suitable for finalisation.
critical_issues: Ambiguous provider_call_audit/condition_counts entry in deterministic_reconciliation.json (appears to list 'shared':500, 'guarded':4) — must be clarified to avoid confusion about per‑condition model‑call accounting.

No concise in‑manuscript table or short appendix summarizing the four repaired/discordant episodes (pair IDs, verifier violation codes, short description of repair prompt or repair outcome); readers should not need to parse raw JSONL to see what was repaired.

Preregistered secondary comparator (templated automation) and associated confirmatory test were not executed. The manuscript must explicitly identify which preregistered hypotheses/confirmatory tests remain untested and clearly state the implications for the preregistered multiplicity (Bonferroni) plan and for interpretation of p‑values/CIs.

Model generation hyperparameters (temperature, max tokens, any sampling or deterministic flags) are not stated in the paper text; the execution artifact contains them but the manuscript must cite these fields and their hashes explicitly.
required_revisions: Clarify provider_call_audit semantics and correct/define the meaning of 'condition_counts' and any apparent mismatch (e.g., why 'guarded' appears as 4). Quote the relevant execution_manifest path and SHA for the clarified field so readers can verify (artifact evidence is available).

Add a concise in‑manuscript table (<=1 small table) listing the four discordant/repaired pair IDs (e.g., pair-000090, pair-000341, pair-000381, pair-000413), the verifier violation codes and short human‑readable descriptions, whether a repair was invoked, model calls used for that pair, and a short anonymized summary of the repair prompt outcome. Use the archived scoring JSON objects (execution/scoring/*.json) and provider traces; cite their artifact paths and SHA(s).

Explicitly state which preregistered confirmatory comparisons were not executed (the templated‑automation arm and H2) and document the practical consequence: the preregistered familywise Bonferroni adjustment cannot be applied as planned. Update the Methods/Abstract wording to reflect that only the primary GVR vs LLM‑only confirmatory comparison was executed and that familywise error control across the originally planned two tests is not applicable.

Insert a one‑sentence explicit listing of model generation settings taken from execution/model_configuration.json (declared_model_version, temperature, max_output_tokens, maximum_attempts_per_call, provider) with artifact SHA (a40e96e2...). If any field is null (e.g., temperature), state that explicitly and explain the effective generator behavior (deterministic/default sampling) as recorded in the artifact.
optional_revisions: Move a brief (1–2 paragraph) summary of the four repaired failure modes from Discussion into Results (or add a small boxed example) so non‑artifact readers can see representative repairs without opening raw artifacts.

Provide the exact artifact path and SHA for the verifier human‑readable codebook (violation‑code → description) inline in the Methods (the execution_manifest already contains this; cite it explicitly).
Add a short per‑difficulty‑level summary (already present in terminal_factual_accounting) as a small table or sentence to help readers assess external validity across task hardness buckets.
Discuss (briefly) whether a one‑sided test would be of operational interest and why the preregistered two‑sided exact conditional McNemar was chosen (short justification).
